chapter_theme: A song at Thiruvaiyaru (திருவையாறு): the poet asks whether the day will come when, leaving the sea of illusion where he praises women part by part, he joins the praise that jnanis sing and reaches the supreme release; the praise names Vishnu's avatars and Siva who is half woman and without caste.

887.reading: The poet gives the lover's questions, is her hair a raining cloud or darkness, are her eyes swords or does, is her speech the gods' nectar or the cuckoo, her gait a swan's or a she-elephant's, her breasts a mountain, and confesses that he talks thus to bright-browed women, saying 'rule me in love, I am without fault', and suffers; he asks whether one day, not perishing in that sea of illusion, he will reach the long praise that jnanis sing, which is the supreme release. The praise names Vishnu the cowherd on the serpent-bed, the Man-Lion who tore Hiranya's chest and Rama who felled Ravana's ten heads with one arrow, as uncle, and Murugan the son of Siva who burned the three cities, has a woman as his half and has no caste, the vel that turned the peak to ash, at Thiruvaiyaru.
887.nuance: ஞானிகள் பரவு நீள்புகழே அது ஆம் மிகு பரம வீடு: the praise itself is equated with release. சாதியிலாதவர்: Siva is named as one without caste or birth. The doubting comparisons of the first half are the stock of akam praise of a woman.

links.note: 887 confesses that he talks to women in doubting comparisons, hair a raining cloud or darkness, eyes swords or does, breasts a mountain, and suffers in a sea of illusion. 372 asks not to spend day and night praising women with hair as darkness that fights the clouds (முகிலை யிகல்பொரு முழுவிருள் குழலென), face as moon, eyes as arrows. The two songs, far apart in the book, make the same confession about the love-poet's similes, and 887's remedy is the praise jnanis sing, called itself release (பரவு நீள்புகழே அது ஆம் மிகு பரம வீடு).
